headline: Why Does My House Still Smell Like Smoke After a Fire?
articleBody: It's super frustrating when you've had a fire, even a small one, and that acrid smoke smell just won't budge. You've cleaned, aired out the place, but it's still there, right? That's because smoke particles are incredibly tiny and intrusive. They don't just sit on surfaces; they get absorbed into just about everything porous in your home. Think about your carpets, curtains, upholstery, even the drywall and wood finishes. These materials act like sponges, soaking up those microscopic smoke residues, and as a result, they continue to release that tell-tale odor over time. Plus, the type of fire makes a big difference. A protein fire, like something burnt in the kitchen, leaves a particularly nasty, difficult-to-remove residue. Even structural components like insulation can harbor these odors for ages. Simply cleaning the visible soot isn't enough; you need to neutralize the odor at its source. Ignoring it can lead to long-term health issues and a persistent, unpleasant living environment.
